steps.title: Saying hello
steps.body:
French has more than one way to say hello. The right one depends on the time of day and on who you are talking to.

In this lesson you learn 5 words. You hear each one, then you use it.

steps.sound: sa-LÜ (round your lips, like saying ee)
steps.exampleEn: Hi! (only with people you know well)

steps.sound: noh (nasal: do not say the n)

steps.explain: Bonsoir means good evening. Use it from the late afternoon on.

steps.prompt: Which greeting is only for friends and family?
steps.explain: Salut is informal. With a stranger, a clinic receptionist or an official, say bonjour.

steps.title: Hello in Canada
steps.body:
In Canada you will also hear allô as a casual hello, especially on the phone.

In Québec shops, people often say bonjour when you leave as well. It is a friendly goodbye, so do not be surprised.

examples.en: hello, and a friendly goodbye in a Québec shop

steps.question: Which greeting did you hear?
steps.explain: Bonsoir ends with the sound swahr: bon-SWAHR.

steps.question: Did you hear yes or no?
steps.explain: Non sounds like noh, with a nasal o. Oui sounds like wee.

steps.prompt: Choose the French word for yes.
steps.explain: Oui means yes. You say wee.

steps.tip: Both syllables are even: bon-JOUR. Say it as if you were walking into a shop.

steps.title: Next: your name
steps.body: In the next lesson you learn the words nom, prénom, français, anglais and Canada. You will need them to fill in forms and to say who you are.
